target: all 9 entry points from Agents A, B and C
mandate: Attack, not plan. Find the cheapest way to discover a plan is wrong before the founder spends weeks on it.

convergence_attack.argument: The rejection was inherited, not derived: the brief said 'Chinese-language product', so all three were told the answer before they reasoned. None priced the countervailing advantage — every payment rail, keyword tool, analytics stack and affiliate program works in English/USD and none works cleanly in RMB for an unlicensed individual. Probably correct on competitive grounds, but reached by obedience, not analysis, so nobody stress-tested it.
convergence_attack.what_a_fourth_agent_would_say: Pick the audience your money can physically reach. If the founder is outside mainland China, an English seasonal product has Stripe, Gumroad, Search Console, Amazon affiliate and email — four attribution and monetization primitives the Chinese plan does not have. Better ONLY if overseas; if mainland, worse than all nine.

convergence_attack.agreement: 小红书 as top-of-funnel discovery surface
convergence_attack.argument: Availability bias dressed as consensus — 小红书 has the highest visible density of food content, so all three saw it first. It is simultaneously the worst channel for this founder's constraint set: zero outbound links, tightening anti-diversion enforcement, no referrer or click data, contact info banned even in auto-replies since Jan 2025, and a Feb 2026 rule requiring 1000 followers / 180 days / 30 notes / ¥6000 monthly GMV before you may sell digital goods at all. Three agents independently choosing the channel where revenue is gated behind the audience you are trying to build is not signal — it is a shared failure to read the rules before choosing the channel.
convergence_attack.what_a_fourth_agent_would_say: Begin only where a link works and a purchase can be counted: 公众号 with 阅读原文 + UTM, 豆瓣 / 一亩三分地 / Dealmoon, Google SEO, or 1:1 outreach. Use 小红书 later as an amplifier, once you know which sentence converts — it is the one channel where you can never learn that. At 10 h/wk, learning rate is the binding constraint, not reach.

convergence_attack.argument: All three reached for the default indie-creator SKU. Nobody did the arithmetic: ¥39 gross minus ~6% 云账户 fee and labour-income withholding is ~¥33-34 net; ¥3,000/month therefore needs ~90 net-new strangers buying every month, forever, sourced from a channel with no clickable link. Seasonality is also the weakest possible thing to charge a consumer for — free on 下厨房, free on 小红书, physically visible at the market stall. The convergence on ¥39 is three agents copying a price point, not three agents pricing a value.
convergence_attack.what_a_fourth_agent_would_say: The price is 10-30x too low and the buyer is wrong. Sell a ¥299-999 quarterly seasonal menu-and-copy pack to people whose money depends on knowing what is in season — 私房菜 kitchens, meal-prep sellers, 社区团购 团长, 生鲜 shops, bakery studios. Ten buyers equals 100+ consumers, the buyer has a budget line, and every prospect is reachable by a direct message with a working link.

convergence_attack.agreement: Founder residence / payment rail is the biggest unknown
convergence_attack.argument: The one genuine convergence, and it indicts the entire output. If three isolated agents independently conclude the plan is undetermined until one binary fact resolves, the correct deliverable was one question and a stop — not nine entry points averaging 8 h/wk. All three then wrote plans anyway, which means roughly half of the nine are known-dead in whichever branch the fact resolves to, and the founder cannot tell which half.
convergence_attack.what_a_fourth_agent_would_say: 'Tell me your country of residence and whether you hold a mainland 身份证, mainland bank card and real-name WeChat. I will not write a plan until you answer, because the answer deletes five of the nine options.' Costs the founder 60 seconds; saves them from executing a plan whose payment rail does not exist.

convergence_attack.agreement: 小报童 is the rail that works for an individual with no Chinese business licence
convergence_attack.argument: Fact-checking refutes the framing. 小报童 is not open registration — creator accounts go through manual one-to-one review, with a reported de-facto bar of ~3,000 cross-platform followers. Payout runs through 云账户, requiring real-name verification against a mainland ID number, mainland bank card and matching phone, ~6% service fee, plus personal income tax withheld as labour remuneration. It substitutes an audience gate and a mainland-identity gate for the licence gate — and both are exactly what this founder lacks.
convergence_attack.what_a_fourth_agent_would_say: For the first twenty buyers use no platform at all: a 微信收款码 or Alipay code plus manual file delivery. Zero gate, zero fee, perfect attribution. Then graduate to 知识星球 (accepts verified individual identity) or 公众号付费阅读 (3-month-old real-name account, 3 原创 articles, ¥1-208 ladder). If overseas, none of these apply — Payhip or Ko-fi with PayPal.

cheapest_kills.test: Submit the 小报童 creator application today with the real account and real follower count. Rejection, or a reply demanding 3,000+ cross-platform followers, kills B3 outright and kills C2 with the same observation. Do this before writing a single column.

Google Keyword Planner (free with any Ads account, no spend), geo US/CA/UK/AU, language Chinese, pull volumes for the 15 head terms the pages would target. Kill if combined addressable monthly volume is under ~500 searches — at a realistic 5-15% CTR that is fewer than 75 visitors/month for 12 weeks of work.

Two observations in one sitting: keyword volume for Chinese queries about Western vegetables, and the structural point that an ingredient explainer is NOT a recipe and does not qualify for Recipe rich results — the JSON-LD premise is wrong, so the differentiation the plan rests on does not exist. Either observation kills it.

Skip the 12 free weeks entirely. Put a $19 pre-order page on Payhip or Ko-fi today (both free, both work without Stripe via PayPal) with an honest 'ships at 秋分' promise, post it in two link-permitting diaspora communities, and see whether one stranger pays within 7 days. Tests willingness-to-pay, the payment rail, and community link tolerance simultaneously.

Post one genuinely useful 处暑 seasonal list into 一亩三分地 and one Douban group with NO link and NO email ask. Two observations at 48 hours: did it survive moderation, and did any human ask a follow-up question. Silence-but-alive means no demand; deletion means no channel.

Search 小红书 in-app for the five target strings and read the top 20 results. Kill if results are mostly domestic-China content or under ~100 收藏 — that means no diaspora-specific demand pool and you would be creating a category, not capturing one. Second free kill: check your own account against the Feb 2026 digital-goods gate.

Same in-app search session as A1 plus three city names. Kill if city-level notes are absent while generic seasonality notes do fine — that proves the city dimension is fake specificity fragmenting an already-thin demand pool into nothing.

Scan the top 20 mainland accounts already posting 菜市场食单 carousels and count how many have any visible monetization. If a saturated niche with far bigger accounts contains nobody selling a ~¥39 pack, the comment-to-WeChat-to-¥39 funnel has been tried and does not clear. Also: contact info in auto-replies and 私信 is a documented violation, so the handoff step is not a risk, it is a rule break.

Identical to B3 — the 小报童 application. Marginal information over B3 is approximately zero, which is exactly the point: C2 is not an independent bet, it is B3 with a price ladder bolted on. Ranking it last is itself a finding — two of nine entry points share a single point of failure.

fact_checks.claim: 小报童 lets an individual with no Chinese business licence collect money, with no meaningful gate
fact_checks.finding: Creator accounts are NOT open registration — manual one-to-one review of creative ability, content quality and update cadence, with a reported de-facto follower bar risen from '1,000 公众号 / 2,000 elsewhere' to roughly 3,000 cross-platform followers. Payouts are not made by 小报童 but through 云账户: creators who have not signed cannot be paid at all; signing verifies name + national ID number + bank card + phone or biometric face check; roughly 6% is taken as service fee; personal income tax is withheld on the remainder as labour remuneration. The licence is indeed not required, but a mainland real-name identity, a mainland bank card and a pre-existing audience effectively are. Unusable as a STARTING rail for a founder with no audience, and likely unusable at all without mainland ID. Caveat: the follower bar comes from Chinese secondary write-ups, not an official published policy page, and may be stale — which is exactly why the application itself is the test.

fact_checks.claim: Stripe cannot serve a mainland-China-resident founder
fact_checks.finding: Stripe does not support launching new accounts for businesses based in mainland China; it is not on the country availability list, so Stripe Atlas is also out of reach without forming an entity elsewhere. The public workaround is a US LLC + EIN + US bank account — a several-hundred-dollar, multi-week detour, out of scope for a $0-cash founder. Note the commonly confused separate fact: Stripe ACCEPTS Alipay and WeChat Pay as customer payment methods for merchants in supported countries. That concerns buyers, not a China-resident seller.

fact_checks.claim: Gumroad / Lemon Squeezy / Paddle / Ko-fi / Payhip are workable alternatives for a mainland-resident founder
fact_checks.finding: Only two of five look plausible. Gumroad: China is not on its payout-country list, pages are slow or blocked behind the Great Firewall, and its PayPal relationship was disrupted in Dec 2024 — not viable. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are merchants of record requiring a payout destination in a supported bank or PayPal country, so viability turns on residence, not product. Ko-fi runs on Stripe or PayPal and inherits the Stripe restriction. Payhip is the most flexible on paper — 13 processors including PayPal, Mollie, Razorpay, Xendit, Paystack — and a PayPal China Platform account exists that lets mainland merchants receive cross-border payments settled in CNY. Bottom line: if mainland-resident, the realistic Western rail is Payhip or Ko-fi backed by PayPal with meaningful friction, and the realistic domestic rail is a plain 微信/支付宝 收款码 with manual delivery, then 知识星球 or 公众号付费阅读. Official supported-country tables were blocked by the proxy — re-confirm in 10 minutes once residence is known.

fact_checks.claim: 小红书 off-platform-diversion penalties are severe, and a profile bio link gets throttled
fact_checks.finding: Verified, and if anything understated by the agents. Strictest-ever diversion governance rules Nov 2024, then a ban on guiding users to off-platform transactions, then Community Convention 2.0 in Jan 2026. From 7 Jan 2025, professional-account auto-reply components and welcome messages are forbidden from containing WeChat IDs or phone numbers; DM diversion is actively pattern-matched on keywords, send frequency and message similarity; penalties escalate from traffic throttling to publishing restrictions to permanent ban, described as effectively unappealable. On bio links: a phone number, WeChat ID, email or URL in the profile bio is treated as a violation or as advertising. An aggregator link is described as safer than raw contact details but not safe, and newly-registered or previously-reported domains get flagged as risky, requiring a manual user confirmation tap that destroys click-through. A bio link is not a clean workaround — it is a throttling risk plus a conversion sink.

fact_checks.claim: The Feb 2026 小红书 digital-goods thresholds are real
fact_checks.finding: Verified across several independent Chinese sources, effective 10 Feb 2026. The 电子资源 gate: 1,000+ followers, ¥6,000+ monthly transaction volume (satisfiable with 12-month history from Taobao/Pinduoduo/Xianyu under the same legal entity), account age 180+ days, 30+ published notes, an individual business licence held 1+ year, or for enterprise stores ¥200,000+ registered capital plus 1+ year of registration, plus a signed compliance undertaking. Two escape hatches: an 成人教育 category requiring teaching or education credentials, and a zero-threshold 个人售卖 route with sharply limited capability and no store. Titles must carry 电子版 or 电子资源; 'lifetime membership' and 'permanent free updates' claims are banned. Practical consequence: A1, B1 and C1 all assume 小红书 can carry a sale, and under this rule a new account cannot legally sell anything digital there for at least six months.

fact_checks.claim: A domestic Chinese rail exists that an individual with no business licence and no audience can open this week
fact_checks.finding: Verified, and none of the three agents proposed it. 知识星球 explicitly accepts verified personal identity in place of a business licence for individual 星主 — qualification materials are submitted before creating a sphere or before withdrawal, and personal real-name identity is accepted. 微信公众号付费阅读 requires only an account registered more than 3 months, no serious violations in the last 3 months, at least 3 articles that passed 原创 declaration, and a real-name verified subject; pricing is a fixed 35-step ladder from ¥1 to ¥208. Both are more accessible to a licence-less mainland individual than 小报童, and 公众号付费阅读 additionally gives per-article conversion data — real attribution, which 小红书 structurally cannot provide. Neither has a follower gate comparable to 小报童's.

fact_checks.claim: There is measurable Chinese-language Google demand for region-by-month seasonal queries (A3) and Chinese explainers of Western vegetables (B2)
fact_checks.finding: Could not check. Chinese-language keyword volume geo-filtered to North America, the UK, Australia and Singapore is not obtainable from public web search — it requires Google Keyword Planner or Ads data behind an authenticated account. Agent A self-assigned A3 only 0.45 confidence and flagged 'no known query volume'; Agent B gave B2 0.40. This is the single largest unverified quantity in the entire nine-plan set, and it is free to resolve: Keyword Planner access costs nothing and takes under an hour. Nobody should write 60-120 pages before that hour is spent.

unasked_question.question: Why are we selling seasonality information to the person for whom it is free, obvious and low-stakes — instead of to the person who loses money every week by getting it wrong?
unasked_question.why_it_matters: All nine plans assume the buyer is a home cook. A home cook can see what is in season by walking past the stall, gets the same information free from 下厨房, 豆果, 小红书 and a hundred 公众号, and suffers no measurable loss from not knowing. That is the textbook profile of a product with near-zero willingness to pay — which is precisely why all three agents independently landed on ¥39. The price is low because the value is low, not because the market is price-sensitive. Meanwhile there is a group for whom seasonality is a recurring operational input with real money attached: 私房菜 and small restaurant kitchens setting weekly menus, meal-prep and 便当 sellers, 社区团购 团长 writing weekly product copy, bakery studios planning seasonal SKUs, small 生鲜 shops. They buy weekly, already spend money on inputs, will pay ¥299-999 per quarter without a second thought, ten of them equal a hundred consumers, and decisively they can be reached one at a time by direct message with a working link — perfect attribution, no dependence on any algorithm, platform rule or follower threshold.
unasked_question.second_uncomfortable_point: The founder has ~10 h/wk. If this product cannot produce a paying stranger within four weeks, the honest question is not 'which channel' but 'should these ten hours be in this product at all' — and the most monetizable asset a technical solo founder owns is usually the system they built, not the content it emits.
unasked_question.concrete_alternative: Reposition from consumer content to a B2B seasonal operations pack: every 节气 (24 per year, one every ~15 days), a one-page pack containing the 10-15 ingredients peaking that fortnight, 6-8 menu lines built from them with rough food cost, and 3 ready-to-publish 朋友圈/群 captions the buyer can paste. Price ¥199 per quarter (6 节气) or ¥699/year. Twenty buyers is ¥14k/year from a list you can build by hand; a hundred consumer buyers at ¥39 is ¥3.9k and requires an algorithm to cooperate. The content asset is nearly identical to what all nine plans already propose building — the change is who receives it and what they pay.
unasked_question.how_to_test_it_this_week: 处暑 falls on ~23 August, five days out. Build one deliberately ugly 2-page 处暑 pack today (12 ingredients, 6 menu lines, 3 captions — 90 minutes, no design). Identify 10 named small food businesses you can actually reach. Send each one the pack free, individually, with one line: 'I make one of these every 节气 — ¥199 for the next six, want in?' Log every send with date and reply. Three yeses means stop everything else and do this. Zero replies out of ten means the B2B thesis is dead too, and you learned it for ¥0 and three hours instead of twelve weeks.

measurement_trap.explanation: Yes — but not on 小红书, the channel all three agents ranked first. There the funnel is note → comment → DM → nothing: contact details in DMs and auto-replies are a documented violation, bio links are a throttling risk, risky-domain interstitials crush click-through, and there is no referrer, no click count and no note-level conversion data. The best available substitute is a coarse self-reported join key, which loses most of the signal and cannot tell you which NOTE worked, only which platform. At 10 h/wk that distinction is decisive: without note-level feedback you cannot iterate content, so you are not running an experiment, you are buying lottery tickets. Honest attribution IS available elsewhere at zero cost: 公众号 gives per-article read counts and a UTM-taggable 阅读原文 link, and 付费阅读 reports conversion per article; 豆瓣, 一亩三分地 and Dealmoon permit real outbound links so UTMs work end to end; Google SEO gives Search Console query-to-page plus a conversion event; email gives per-send click and purchase data; and 1:1 outreach gives 100% attribution by construction. The plans inverted the ordering — they ranked channels by reach and treated attribution as a risk footnote, when at this scale attribution is the product.
measurement_trap.which_channel_should_be_first: Direct 1:1 outreach first (perfect attribution, zero platform risk, tests willingness-to-pay directly rather than through a reach proxy), with a WeChat 公众号 as the owned, linkable, measurable asset built in parallel, and one or two link-permitting communities as the only broadcast channel in month one. 小红书 moves to month three at the earliest, as an amplifier for a message already proven to convert — and only once the account clears the Feb 2026 gate, which takes 180 days anyway, so there is no cost to deferring it.

single_most_dangerous_assumption: That a Chinese-speaking home cook will pay real money for seasonality information that is free, already published by a dozen larger free sources, and physically visible at the market — an assumption every one of the nine plans requires, that all three agents priced at ¥39 without ever testing, and that none of the nine confronts until week six or later. The payment-rail question everyone flagged as the biggest unknown is downstream of it, because a rail you cannot open matters far less than a product nobody was going to buy.
monday_morning: 0:00-0:20 — Write down, in one line, your country of residence and whether you hold a mainland 身份证 + mainland bank card + real-name WeChat. Do not plan past this line. If mainland: rails are a plain 微信收款码 with manual file delivery for the first twenty buyers, then 知识星球 or 公众号付费阅读. If overseas: Payhip or Ko-fi in your country of residence. Open the account NOW — a rail you have not tested is not a rail. 0:20-0:50 — Submit the 小报童 creator application with your real numbers; it is free, takes twenty minutes, and its rejection deletes both B3 and C2 before you write a word. While it is pending, pull Chinese-language Keyword Planner volumes geo-filtered to your target regions for the 15 head terms behind A3 and B2. 0:50-2:20 — Build one deliberately ugly 处暑 pack for 23 August: 12-15 peaking ingredients, 6 menu lines with rough food cost, 3 paste-ready group captions. Two pages, no design pass, no logo, no landing page. 2:20-3:00 — Send it individually and free to 10 named small food businesses you can already reach, each with one line: 'I make one every 节气; ¥199 for the next six.' Log all ten with a unique code per recipient. At the end of three hours you have: the rail answered and open, two entry points killed for free, the SEO volume question resolved, and ten attribution-clean willingness-to-pay conversations running — strictly more information than any of the nine plans produces in its first month, for three hours and zero dollars. Do not open 小红书 at all this week.
